text:
**False.**

The Great Wall of China is not visible from space (low Earth orbit or beyond, such as the Moon) with the naked eye under normal conditions. It is only a few meters wide, follows the terrain, and lacks strong contrast with the surrounding landscape, so it does not stand out to unaided vision. Astronauts (including those on the ISS and Apollo missions) and agencies such as NASA have repeatedly confirmed it cannot be reliably seen without magnification or ideal lighting/angles that still do not make it obvious. 

High-resolution photos or telescopic views can capture sections, but that is not naked-eye visibility. The popular claim is a long-standing myth; many other human features (cities, roads, airports) are far easier to spot from orbit.
